newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Bukavu archbishop killed in Zaire, priests say.
newsitem.headline: Bukavu archbishop killed in Zaire, priests say.

text.p: The Roman Catholic archbishop of the eastern Zairean town of Bukavu has been killed, priests in Burundi said on Wednesday.
The priests in the Burundian capital Bujumbura said they heard the news of the killing of Archbishop Muziriwa, a Zairean Jesuit, relayed from fellow priests in Bukavu but gave few details.
"Catholic missionaries in Bukavu told us by radio the Archbishop of Bukavu, Bishop Muziriwa, had been killed," an Italian Catholic priest in Bujumbura told Reuters on Wednesday.
"The missionaries said it was impossible to go out because of the possibility of being shot and they were staying in their house," the priest said, adding Muziriwa was not an ethnic Tutsi.
Bukavu, the capital of South Kivu province, has been under attack from ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels and Zairean troops have been on a looting spree and robbing foreigners in recent days.
On Wednesday evening it was not clear who was in charge of Bukavu, Zairean troops or rebels.

"We have field reports that Bukavu has fallen and that Rwandan commandos are now there, but we have no independent confirmation," said one aid worker in Geneva. Western agencies have pulled out of Bukavu due to insecurity.
